How it works

Who is accountable, who decides and what proof remains.

Every organisation already has areas that produce data and people who depend on it. The KDV operating model gives this a name. Explore each part without leaving this page.

Business domain

The business area accountable for the meaning and priorities of a set of data.

Has a named owner, coordinates its subdomains and respects the ecosystem's common baseline. It need not match the organisation chart: it follows who decides on the meaning of the data.

Example

Finance; Customer service; Professional registration; Inspection.

Domain owner — Accountable for the domain; sponsors the use case and decides escalated approvals.

Coordinating steward — Coordinates the stewards' work and resolves questions across subdomains.

What shows this concept exists in practice:

  • Domain charter
  • Named owner
  • Domain glossary

In the market: Data domain · business domain (Data Mesh)

In KDV: Hive

Why this name? The hive: an autonomous unit with its own organisation that contributes to the whole.

Reference interfaces

Consumer, Producer, EcOps and PlatOps in one line.

These are the screens of the reference implementation, organised by who uses them. They do not replace roles.

Share · Activate

KDV Consumer

Those who find and use data. Catalogue, time-limited access requests, contract reading and tracking of grants.

Cultivate · Govern · Share

KDV Producer

Those who prepare and publish data. Domains, subdomains, contracts, versions, quality and decisions on access requests.

Govern

KDV EcOps

Those who govern the ecosystem. Common policies, governance profiles, roles, forum decisions and indicators.

Shared foundation

KDV PlatOps

Those who operate the platform. Environments, services, alerts, certificates and secrets, without showing their values.

Activate

KDV Desk

Everyone. Common desk for questions, problems and data incidents.

Shared foundation

Adapters

Platform engineering. Connect the model to the chosen tools, without separate product versions.

AI, GDPR and LGPD

Data for AI with explicit limits of use.

A catalogue entry or an AI connector is not enough. Governance applies to the purpose, the inputs, the outputs and the human decisions.

01

Purpose and authority

Record the intended use and who may authorise it. A new AI use may require a new decision.

02

Minimisation and access

Limit data and privileges to what is needed, including search and derived results.

03

Origin and evaluation

Record sources, freshness and limitations; evaluate the quality of the answers.

04

People and rights

Plan for review, challenge, incidents and data subjects' rights (GDPR/LGPD).
